what: Fan-out protocol mandates one shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR across concurrent worktree cargo/task invocations. After introducing a real type error (E0308) in a worktree, repeated `cargo test` runs against the shared dir kept printing a clean 'Finished ... Ns' + a stale, wrong pass count (14, from before the edit) with no error text at all — never the compiler error, never the correct post-fix count. Only pointing CARGO_TARGET_DIR at an isolated, worktree-local dir surfaced the real compile error and, after the fix, the correct test count; the same command against the shared dir then also reported correctly.
tell: cargo test against the shared target dir reports a suspiciously stable pass count that does not change across edits (e.g. new #[test] fns never appear in --list), with no compiler error shown despite a real one existing; a one-off build against an isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR in the same worktree shows the true result immediately
proposed_change: when a shared-target-dir cargo result looks stale or inconsistent with a just-made edit (test count unchanged, --list missing a just-added test), do not trust it — rerun once against a throwaway worktree-local CARGO_TARGET_DIR to get ground truth before concluding the code is broken or wasting more retries on the shared dir
evidence: fu/opencode-agent-values worktree, shared dir /home/mherwig/dev/grimoire/.agents/worktrees/.fu-target: `cargo test --bin grim vendor_opencode` repeatedly reported 'cargo test: 14 passed' (pre-edit count) after a fix + 4 new tests were added; an isolated target dir in the same worktree correctly showed the E0308 compile error, then 18 passed after the fix
